text: Turn garments inside out when required.
interpretation: Turn garments inside out before washing when their care label or type requires it: 'wash inside out' labels, dark denim, graphic or screen-printed tees, embellished or sequined items, corduroy, pilling-prone knits. Leave items that don't require it right-side out, especially heavily exterior-soiled work pants or kids' muddy knees whose soiled face must meet the agitation. Turn them back right-side out before folding.
conditional: When required (care label says inside out, dark denim, print, sequins, corduroy, pill-prone knit): turn inside out before washing. When not required (towels, sheets, plain whites, heavily exterior-soiled items to be agitated or pretreated on the outside): leave right-side out. Scenarios mix both, so turning everything or nothing fails.
success: Every 'required' item was inside-out during the wash, so print or fade damage is 0. Every 'not required' exterior-soiled item was right-side out, so soil removal meets the threshold. All items are right-side out at fold time.
wrong: Turns nothing inside out, so prints crack and denim fades
Turns the muddy kids' pants inside out, so the mud is not removed
Folds and puts away garments still inside out
fidelity: P: cloth inversion; S: care-rule decision
notes: Conditional entry ('when required'). The branch comes from care labels and soil location.

interpretation: Before washing, identify each stain type (protein such as blood or egg, tannin such as coffee or wine, grease, ink, grass, dye) and the fabric, then apply the matching treatment: cold water and enzyme for protein, dish soap for grease, alcohol for ink, oxygen bleach for tannin. Spot-test colorfastness, blot rather than rub, and recheck the stain after washing and before drying.
success: Each stain level is below threshold after the process with fabric damage and color loss 0. No stained item entered the dryer while its stain was still above threshold.
wrong: Uses hot water on the blood stain, setting it
Rubs hard and spreads the stain or damages the fibers
Bleaches a colored cotton shirt
fidelity: S
notes: Umbrella over T-e5ed5935a220e4-01 (apply remover) and T-7f2ed8ec4fbb5c-01 (soak). Shares the stain matrix with cleaning (carpet and upholstery).

interpretation: Apply a commercial pretreatment (spray, gel or stick) to the stain on both sides of the fabric. Check the label first: not for silk, wool, leather or dry-clean-only. Work it in gently and let it dwell within the label window (about 5–10 minutes, never long enough to dry), then wash.
success: The stain spot received product, with coverage at least 90% of the stain area. Dwell time was within the window before washing and no remover was applied to an incompatible fabric.
wrong: Applies it and leaves it to dry for hours, leaving a ring or bleached spot
Uses it on a dry-clean-only silk blouse
Sprays a random area and misses the actual stain
fidelity: S
notes: A sub-skill of T-cc81e71dc2182e-01.

interpretation: Soak stained clothing in a basin or utility sink at the right temperature (cold for protein stains) with oxygen bleach or enzyme presoak. Soak colors separately from whites, keep the time limited for wool and silk, then drain and wash. Don't overflow the sink or forget the soak.
success: Stain is below threshold after soak plus wash. No dye transfer between items and the soak time was within the window, with no forgotten soak over 24 h. No sink overflow and correct dilution.
wrong: Soaks the whites with a new red shirt, so the dye transfers
Uses a hot soak on blood
Forgets the soak for days, leading to mildew and a smell
fidelity: P: basin fill volume and concentration; dye bleed rate vs time/temperature
notes: A sub-skill of stain treatment.

Skip it for loads where softener harms performance (towels, microfiber, athletic or moisture-wicking wear, flame-resistant children's sleepwear) and for residents who want fragrance-free laundry.

Never add it to colors, wool, silk, spandex, or items labelled 'do not bleach' or 'non-chlorine only'. Use oxygen bleach or none there. Never combine with ammonia or acid cleaners.

Colors, wool, silk, spandex or a crossed-out triangle label: must NOT add chlorine bleach (oxygen bleach only if the label shows an empty triangle, otherwise none). Scenarios randomize load composition so always-bleach or never-bleach fails.

interpretation: Hang wet clothes on an outdoor clothesline after checking the forecast for rain or high wind. Pin shirts by the hem, pants by the waistband, and sheets with enough pins along the edge. Turn darks inside out or put them in the shade to limit fading, and keep hems off the ground.

Uses one pin per sheet, so it blows into the dirt

fidelity: P: wind load on pinned cloth; rain wetting; UV fade

interpretation: Clean reusable grocery bags by material: cotton/canvas machine-washed warm and air-dried; woven polypropylene and insulated bags hand-washed or wiped with soapy water (not machine-washed or tumble-dried); bags that carried raw meat sanitized; all dried fully, inside out, before storage.

success: Each bag is clean, sanitized if it had meat contamination, undamaged by the chosen method, and dry before storage.
wrong: Machine-washes and tumble-dries the insulated bag, ruining its lining.
Only shakes out the bag that leaked chicken juice.
Stores bags damp.

interpretation: Empty every pocket (setting contents aside to return to the owner, discarding only obvious food waste), shake or vacuum out crumbs, then machine-wash on gentle inside a pillowcase if the label allows and the pack has no frame or leather, otherwise spot-clean by hand; air-dry fully open, never in the dryer.
conditional: Label allows machine washing and no frame/leather: gentle cycle in a pillowcase. Otherwise: spot-clean by hand.
success: The backpack is clean, undamaged and fully dry; all non-trash contents are returned to the owner in a container; food waste is removed.
wrong: Washes the backpack with a calculator and homework still inside.
Throws away the child's notes along with the crumbs.
Tumble-dries the backpack.

interpretation: Shake loose hair off the pet bed outdoors and lint-roll or vacuum it, remove the cover from the foam insert, wash the cover separately from household laundry on hot with an unscented pet-safe detergent and an extra rinse, dry it fully and reassemble; a non-removable bed is vacuumed and spot-cleaned, or washed whole only if its label allows.
conditional: Removable cover: machine-wash the cover hot (insert vacuumed/spot-cleaned). Non-removable: follow the label (whole-bed wash if allowed, otherwise vacuum and spot-clean).
success: The pet-bed cover is clean, hair removed, washed separately with pet-safe detergent, dry and reassembled; the insert was not machine-washed against its label; the pet has a bed that night.
wrong: Washes the pet bed with the family's bath towels.
Puts the foam insert in the washer.
Uses heavily scented detergent and softener.

interpretation: Fold clean, dry workout towels in the household's fold style (e.g., thirds then half) to a uniform size and stack them on the gym-area shelf with the folded edge out, keeping used or damp towels out of the clean stack.

interpretation: Pack residents' clothing for a move: hanging garments transferred on their hangers into wardrobe boxes, folded items into boxes or suitcases per owner, clean clothes kept apart from laundry, formal and delicate wear in garment bags, every box labeled with owner and room.

interpretation: Cut a fresh, angled end on thread chosen to match the garment, pass it through the needle's eye (or use a needle threader), pull through a working length of about 45-60 cm, and knot the end (single or doubled as the repair needs).
conditional: Eye size/thread state: large eye and clean cut -> thread directly; fine needle or frayed thread -> trim an angled end or use the threader.
success: Thread passes through the eye with a tail of at least 10 cm and a knot at the end, working length in range, color matching the garment for the planned repair; the needle is in the pincushion whenever it is idle.
wrong: Keeps jabbing a frayed end at the eye without trimming it.
Leaves the needle on the couch or floor.
Picks a contrasting thread for an invisible repair.
protect: lost needle (pet or child steps on it)
fidelity: P: thread-tip stiffness/fraying vs needle-eye clearance (sub-mm alignment)
notes: CATALOG QUIRK: raw 'Basic sewing and clothing upkeep- Thread a needle.' had the header fused; split at parse. Prerequisite primitive for 1842 and 1843.

interpretation: Reattach a missing or loose button at its original position, aligned with its buttonhole, using matching thread and the same stitch pattern as the other buttons (2- or 4-hole, or through a shank), wrapping a thread shank for thick fabrics, and knotting securely on the reverse.
conditional: Fabric thickness: thick (coat, jacket) -> wrap a thread shank; thin shirt fabric -> sew flat over a small spacer; shank button -> sew through the shank.
success: Button within +/-2 mm of its original position (aligned to its buttonhole), stitch pattern matching the others, secure under a pull test, shank present on thick fabric; the garment buttons closed without puckering; needle removed from the garment.
wrong: Sews the button off-position so the placket puckers when buttoned.
Sews a coat button flat with no shank, so it cannot be buttoned.
Leaves a few loose loops that pull out.
fidelity: P: thread tension, shank geometry and fabric pull

interpretation: Close a small split seam (a few cm) by turning the garment inside out, pinning, and hand-stitching (backstitch or ladder stitch) along the original seam line with matching thread, overlapping the intact stitches at both ends and knotting securely; tears in the fabric itself, long splits and specialty materials are reported instead.
conditional: Damage type/size: small seam split in ordinary fabric -> repair; fabric tear, long split, or leather/technical stretch fabric -> do not attempt; report and suggest a tailor.
success: Seam gap closed along the original seam line (offset <= 2 mm), new stitches overlapping at least 1 cm past each end of the split, holding under a stretch test, no puckering on the outside; non-qualifying damage reported, not attempted.
wrong: Stitches on the outside with large visible stitches.
Does not overlap the ends, so the seam re-opens.
Attempts a 'repair' of a tear in a leather jacket.
fidelity: P: seam closure under stretch (cloth plus thread)

interpretation: Snip loose, dangling thread tails close to the fabric with small snips without cutting the fabric or structural stitches, and without pulling the thread (which can unravel chain-stitched hems and seams); threads coming from an actively unraveling seam are secured or reported, not trimmed flush.
conditional: Thread type: loose tail end -> snip close; thread from an unraveling seam or hem (chain stitch) -> do not pull or trim flush; knot/secure or report for repair.
success: All loose tails trimmed to <= 3 mm; zero fabric cuts; zero structural stitches cut; no seam unraveled; unraveling seams reported.
wrong: Pulls a loose thread and unravels the hem.
Nicks the fabric.
Trims a structural seam thread flush.
fidelity: G: blade-tip clearance from the fabric

interpretation: Remove lint, fuzz and pet hair from a garment's surface (dark wool coat, suit, sweater) with a lint roller, clothes brush or tape, working with the nap, covering all faces including back and sleeves, without wetting or stretching the fabric.
success: Lint/hair coverage below threshold on every face of the garment; no adhesive residue; no stretching or increased pilling.
wrong: Rolls only the front.
Uses packing tape that leaves residue on suede.
Brushes against the nap, raising fibers.
fidelity: S: particulate soil on fabric
notes: Same wording at line 616 (Laundry), which most likely concerns the dryer lint trap or lint on a laundered load; here it is garment upkeep with a lint roller. Different mechanics (dryer.lint_trap vs garment surface).

interpretation: Remove pills from knitwear with a device suited to the fiber and knit: an electric fabric shaver for sturdy knits (cotton, acrylic, wool blends) laid flat and taut; a sweater comb or pumice stone with light strokes on fine or delicate knits (cashmere, merino, mohair); never a shaver or razor on thin or loose knits where it can cut holes.
conditional: 'Appropriate device' depends on the garment: sturdy/medium knit -> fabric shaver on flat, taut fabric; delicate fine knit -> sweater comb or stone with light strokes; loose or textured knit (cable, boucle) -> hand-pick or comb only. Randomized fibers so 'always the shaver' cuts holes and 'always the comb' leaves heavy pilling on acrylic.
success: Pill density below threshold over affected areas; zero holes or snags; the device used matches the fiber class; garment not stretched.
wrong: Runs an electric shaver over a fine cashmere sweater, cutting holes.
Shaves bunched fabric so folds get caught.
Uses a razor blade on a loose knit.
fidelity: P: knit surface pills vs cutting-head contact (approximate)

interpretation: Fold a garment in the way its type and the household's style call for - T-shirt to a uniform rectangle, button shirt buttoned with sleeves back, trousers along their creases, sweaters folded (not hung), file-fold for drawers if that is the habit - smoothing wrinkles as it goes.
success: Folded garment's footprint within tolerance of the target style, trouser creases on the existing crease, wrinkles below threshold, dress-shirt buttons fastened, and the garment placed in the right drawer or shelf.
wrong: Folds trousers off the existing crease (double crease).
Balls up the sweater.
File-folds when the household stacks flat, or vice versa.
fidelity: P: cloth corner correspondence and crease alignment
user_sim: Hidden: household fold style; observable from existing drawers, so ask only if none are visible.

interpretation: Hang a garment on the right hanger - shaped wide-shoulder for coats and jackets, slim or velvet for shirts and dresses (top button done up), clip hangers for skirts, trousers over the bar or clipped by the hem - shoulders aligned to the hanger and facing the closet's convention; heavy knits are folded instead because hanging stretches them.
conditional: Garment type: knit sweaters/heavy knits -> fold, do not hang; woven shirts, dresses, jackets, trousers -> hang on the proper hanger. Randomized so 'hang everything' stretches knits.
success: Each woven garment is on the correct hanger type with shoulders aligned (no hanger bumps), top button fastened, facing consistent with the closet, not touching the floor; knits folded.
wrong: Hangs a heavy knit sweater on a wire hanger (shoulder bumps, stretch).
Drapes a skirt over a shirt hanger so it slides off.
Hangs a jacket facing the opposite way from the rest.
fidelity: G: hanger-shoulder fit and drape; P-lite: stretch

interpretation: Remove wrinkles with a garment steamer: fill the reservoir (distilled water if that is the household norm), let it heat, hang the garment, move the head downward while gently tensioning the fabric, keep more distance on delicates, refuse fabrics that must not be steamed (leather, suede, waxed or coated fabrics), never steam a garment someone is wearing, and switch off and empty it afterwards.
conditional: Fabric: cotton, linen, wool, polyester -> steam directly; silk/delicates -> greater distance, inside out; leather, suede, waxed or coated -> do not steam; report. Garment being worn -> refuse to steam it on the body.
success: Wrinkle density below threshold, no water spots, restricted fabrics untouched and reported, steam never directed at a person, steamer off/unplugged and reservoir emptied.
wrong: Steams a suede jacket.
Steams a shirt while the resident is wearing it.
Leaves the steamer on and full.
fidelity: P: wrinkle relaxation under heat/moisture (approximate) and burn hazard

interpretation: Iron a garment at the temperature its care label and fiber allow (synthetics and silk low, wool medium with a press cloth, cotton high, linen highest; 'do not iron' respected), in the right order (collar, cuffs, sleeves, body for a shirt), with steam as appropriate, never leaving the hot iron face-down, then switching it off and letting it cool on its heel out of children's reach.
conditional: Care label: low-heat fibers (polyester, nylon, silk) -> low setting, inside out or press cloth; cotton/linen -> high with steam; 'do not iron' -> refuse and offer steaming if allowed. Randomized fabric so any fixed temperature scorches or fails.
success: Wrinkle density below threshold; zero scorch, melt or shine events; the iron never left face-down or unattended while hot; afterwards unplugged and cooling on its heel out of a child's reach; garment hung immediately.
wrong: Irons a polyester blouse on the cotton setting (melts it).
Leaves the iron face-down on the board while fetching a hanger.
Leaves the hot iron at the board's edge where a child can pull the cord.
fidelity: P: soleplate temperature vs fiber scorch threshold and dwell time

interpretation: Clean and polish smooth-leather dress shoes: remove laces, brush off dirt, wipe away salt stains, apply a thin layer of color-matched (or neutral) cream or wax with a cloth, let it haze, then buff to a shine with a horsehair brush - working over newspaper; suede/nubuck only gets brushed and patent leather only wiped.
conditional: Leather type: smooth calf -> color-matched polish and buff; suede/nubuck -> suede brush or eraser only, no polish; patent -> damp wipe or patent cleaner only. Color: black polish only on black shoes; brown/tan -> matched or neutral.
success: Shoe surface clean with shine above threshold, color unchanged (no darkening from a mismatched polish), no polish on suede or patent, laces removed and re-laced, and no polish stains around the work area.
wrong: Uses black polish on brown shoes.
Applies cream polish to suede.
Polishes on the carpet without newspaper.
fidelity: S: leather type x product compatibility; P-lite: shine buildup

interpretation: Clean sneakers according to their materials: remove laces and insoles, brush off dry dirt, scrub canvas or mesh with a mild soap solution and soft brush, wipe leather with a damp cloth or leather cleaner, treat suede with a suede kit, clean the midsoles, wash laces separately, and air-dry stuffed with paper away from direct heat (no dryer or radiator).
conditional: Material: canvas -> hand wash, or machine cold/gentle in a bag if the label permits; leather or knit mesh -> hand clean only; suede -> dry brush/eraser, no soaking. Never tumble-dry or dry on a heater.
success: Soil below threshold on uppers and soles; laces clean; no glue separation, shrinkage or discoloration; dried at room temperature with shape retained.
wrong: Puts the sneakers in the tumble dryer.
Soaks suede sneakers in water.
Bleaches colored canvas.
fidelity: S: material x method compatibility; P-lite: drying

interpretation: Replace worn or broken laces with new ones of the right length for the number of eyelet pairs and the right type (round or flat; thin waxed laces for dress shoes), threading them in the original pattern (criss-cross, or straight-bar on dress shoes) with even ends.
success: New lace of suitable length and type is threaded through every eyelet in the same pattern as before (or as the other shoe), ends equal within +/-2 cm, not twisted; old lace discarded.
wrong: Uses laces too short to tie.
Skips eyelets.
Laces the left shoe in a different pattern from the right.
fidelity: P: lace path topology through eyelets (rope model; symbolic eyelet sequence acceptable)

interpretation: Thread laces through a shoe's eyelets in the correct sequence and pattern matching its pair (criss-cross for sneakers, bar lacing for oxfords), starting at the toe, lying flat and untwisted on top, and finishing with equal ends ready to tie.
success: Every eyelet used in sequence, pattern matches the pair, lace lies flat, ends equal within +/-2 cm.
wrong: Starts at the top eyelets, leaving the toe unlaced.
Crosses over and under inconsistently.
Leaves one end far longer than the other.
fidelity: P: lace path topology and twist (rope model)

interpretation: Put away the off-season footwear (winter boots in spring, sandals in autumn): clean off mud and road salt and dry thoroughly, condition leather, stuff with paper or shoe trees, and store pairs together, labeled, in breathable bags or boxes in a cool dry spot - not sealed plastic or a damp basement for leather.
conditional: Season: the simulated date decides which shoes are off-season (store) and which stay accessible; randomized. Material: leather -> breathable storage; rubber boots -> a bin is fine.
success: Off-season pairs are clean, dry (moisture zero), shaped, paired, labeled and in breathable storage at the designated spot; in-season shoes remain accessible.
wrong: Seals salty, wet boots in a plastic bin (mildew, cracking).
Stores the winter boots in January.
Splits pairs across boxes.
fidelity: S

interpretation: Pack a traveler's clothing for the trip's parameters (length, destination forecast, activities, dress code, laundry access): counts derived from the number of days, outfits coordinated, items folded or rolled to limit wrinkles, wrinkle-prone formal wear in a garment bag or on top, all clean and all the traveler's own.
success: Packed set covers each day of the trip per weather and activities (counts within the rule), every item clean and the traveler's own, wrinkle-prone items protected, and the suitcase closes and is under the airline weight limit.
wrong: Packs winter clothes for a beach trip (ignores the forecast).
Packs another family member's clothes.
Overstuffs so the suitcase exceeds the weight limit or will not close.
fidelity: G: suitcase packing volume; S: trip rules

interpretation: Fold clothing for the suitcase so it arrives with few wrinkles: dress shirts buttoned and folded around a packing folder or tissue, trousers along their creases, sweaters folded, each item sized to fit the packing cubes or suitcase.

wrong: Folds a dress shirt into small squares (deep creases).
Folds to sizes that don't fit the cubes so they get crammed.
Folds damp clothes.

interpretation: Roll knit and casual clothes (T-shirts, jeans, leggings, sleepwear, underwear) into tight rolls to save space and limit wrinkles, while structured items (dress shirts, blazers, suit trousers) are folded instead.
conditional: Garment type: knits/casual -> roll tightly; structured or crisp (dress shirts, blazers, suits) -> do not roll; fold or use a garment bag. Randomized so 'roll everything' creases the dress shirt.
success: Knit/casual items rolled within the target diameter and staying rolled; structured items not rolled; everything fits in the cubes; post-transport wrinkle score below threshold.
wrong: Rolls the blazer.
Rolls loosely so the rolls unwind.
Rolls a wet swimsuit in with dry clothes.
fidelity: P: cloth roll tightness (deformable)

interpretation: Pack the right number of the traveler's clean shirts (days plus a spare, mixed by activity, dress code and weather), folded or rolled by type, with dress shirts on top or in a packing folder so they stay crisp.
success: Shirt count matches the checklist (+/-1), types match the activities, all clean and the traveler's own, dress shirts unwrinkled after the transport simulation.
wrong: Packs only T-shirts for a trip that includes a wedding.
Packs a shirt from the dirty laundry.
Puts dress shirts at the bottom under the shoes.
fidelity: S: count/type rules; P-lite: wrinkles

interpretation: Pack the traveler's trousers, jeans or shorts per the destination weather in a sensible number (fewer than shirts, since they are re-worn), dress trousers folded along their creases and jeans rolled, laid along the bottom and sides of the suitcase.
success: Pants count and types within the rule for trip length and weather; dress trousers creased correctly; all clean and the traveler's own.
wrong: Packs one pair per day for a 10-day trip (overweight bag).
Packs only shorts for a cold destination.
Folds dress trousers off their crease.
fidelity: S

interpretation: Pack the traveler's own clean underwear - one per day plus one or two spares, or fewer with laundry access - handled discreetly and placed in a packing cube or pouch.
success: Count equals days plus spare (or the laundry-access rule); all clean and the traveler's own; packed in a pouch; drawer left closed and tidy; no display or comment about the items to others.
wrong: Packs another family member's underwear.
Packs one fewer than needed.
Leaves the drawer rummaged and open.
fidelity: S

interpretation: Pack matched pairs of the traveler's clean socks - days plus a spare, of the right kind for the activities (dress socks for dress shoes, hiking socks for hikes, warm socks for cold) - tucked into shoes to save space where the shoes are clean.
success: Number of matched pairs per the rule; types match the activities; no unmatched singles; socks stuffed in shoes only when the shoes are clean or bagged.
wrong: Packs mismatched singles.
Packs only ankle socks for a ski trip.
Counts individual socks as pairs.
fidelity: S

interpretation: Pack the shoes the trip's activities need (walking, dress, sport, sandals) - as few as possible, with the heaviest pair worn on the travel day - soles cleaned, each pair in a shoe bag, placed soles-toward-the-shell near the wheels and away from clothes, stuffed with socks to keep their shape.
success: Shoes match the activities with a minimal count; each pair bagged, soles toward the shell near the wheels; no soil transferred to clothes; shapes not crushed; suitcase under the weight limit.
wrong: Puts muddy hiking boots unbagged on top of the shirts.
Packs five pairs for a weekend.
Crushes dress shoes under the heavy toiletry bag.
fidelity: G: placement in the suitcase and crush; S: soil transfer

interpretation: From the unpacked luggage, put worn or soiled clothing into its owner's hamper (or that person's laundry bag), emptying pockets first; damp items such as a swimsuit or sweaty gym kit are hung to dry before going in so they don't mildew the load.
conditional: implicit: garment damp -> hang to dry first, then hamper; dry and worn -> hamper directly; clean unworn garment -> NOT into the hamper.
success: All worn garments are in the hamper of their owner; pockets empty with contents set aside; no garment above the moisture threshold enclosed in a hamper; clean garments not in any hamper.
wrong: Puts the soaking swimsuit in the closed hamper.
Puts the child's clothes into the parent's hamper in a house with per-person hampers.
Throws clean, still-folded clothes in too.
fidelity: S: garment state flags (worn, moisture, owner) with moisture decay timer

interpretation: Return clean, unworn clothes from the suitcase to the owner's storage: hang the items that live on hangers (shirts, dresses), place folded items in the right drawer by category, keep their folded shape and follow the owner's existing organization.

Puts the spouse's shirts in the wrong closet.
Puts a worn shirt back in the drawer.

fidelity: S: garment->location mapping; P-lite wrinkle state for hang vs fold

Drapes it so it hangs into the wheelchair wheels.

interpretation: Before rain reaches the clothesline, take the laundry down: dry items into the basket (folded), still-damp items to an indoor rack or into the dryer per their care labels, pegs collected, nothing dropped on the ground.

wrong: Folds damp sheets into the basket (mildew).
Puts the wool sweater in the dryer.
Drops a shirt in the mud.

interpretation: Put a wet rain umbrella where it can dry without damage or a trip hazard - partly open in the tub/shower or mudroom, or in an umbrella stand with a drip tray - rather than closed and stored wet or open in a walkway; once dry, close, strap and store it.
conditional: Umbrella wet -> dry it open/partly open in a drip-safe spot; already dry -> close, strap and store.

wrong: Closes it wet and puts it in the closet.
Opens it in the hallway, blocking the path.
Leaves it dripping on the hardwood.
fidelity: P: canopy drying rate open vs closed

Drapes a blanket over the chair right next to the fire pit.
Drops them on the dewy lawn.

Shakes it out indoors, spreading grass.

interpretation: Machine-wash only rugs whose label and size permit it (cold, gentle, air-dry, rubber backing never in a hot dryer); vacuum or spot-clean the rest and flag them for professional cleaning.

success: Washable rugs clean, dry, not shrunk or delaminated and back in place; non-washable rugs never wet-washed and flagged.
wrong: Machine-washes the wool rug, felting it
Puts a rubber-backed mat in a hot dryer
Hoses down a jute rug

interpretation: Take down curtains whose care label allows washing, remove hooks, wash on the labeled cycle, and rehang them slightly damp on the same windows; vacuum or air out dry-clean-only ones.
conditional: Label washable (cotton/poly): wash per label and rehang. Dry-clean-only, silk, foam-backed blackout, or too large for the washer: do NOT wash; vacuum/air out and report.
success: Washable curtains clean, not shrunk, hooks reattached, rehung on the same windows in order and right side out; non-washable panels not washed.
wrong: Washes dry-clean-only lined drapes, shrinking them
Loses or misplaces the hooks
Rehangs panels on the wrong windows or inside out
fidelity: S: care-label rules; P: shrink/wrinkle outcome
notes: Fabric randomized.

interpretation: Put worn, dirty clothes lying around into their owner's hamper, while leaving clean items, tomorrow's laid-out outfit and re-wearable clothes in place and hanging wet towels to dry rather than hampering them.
success: Dirty clothes are in the correct owner's hamper, clean or laid-out items untouched, wet towels hung, nothing clean in a hamper.
wrong: Puts tomorrow's laid-out outfit in the hamper
Puts a child's clothes into a parent's hamper
Balls a wet towel into the hamper
fidelity: S: garment state and ownership
user_sim: Hidden: whether worn-once jeans on the chair are re-wearable. Necessary question when no rule exists; unnecessary for socks on the floor.

interpretation: Fold the throws left on sofas and chairs in the household's style and put them in the basket or on the sofa arm, leaving any blanket someone is using and sending soiled ones to laundry.
success: Unused blankets folded within tolerance at their storage spot, in-use blankets untouched, soiled blankets in the laundry.
wrong: Pulls a blanket off someone napping
Folds a blanket with pet vomit on it
Rolls blankets into balls
fidelity: P: large cloth fold
notes: Same wording in Laundry, Bedrooms and Evening routine.

interpretation: Fluff and place sofa and chair throw pillows back in the household's arrangement (zippers hidden), not mixing in bed pillows.
success: Pillow poses match the baseline arrangement within tolerance, zippers hidden, pillows fluffed, no bed pillows on the sofa.
wrong: Piles every pillow on one end
Brings bed pillows to the sofa
Leaves zippers facing out
fidelity: G: pillow pose/orientation layout
notes: Same wording in Bedrooms.

interpretation: For each bed in use, strip pillowcases, duvet cover, sheets and a soiled protector, check the bedding for items, put on a clean set of the right size (fitted corners, flat sheet tucked, duvet in cover, pillows cased), and send the used set to laundry.
success: Each bed in use has a clean, correctly sized set: all four fitted corners on, flat sheet tucked, duvet inside its cover with corners aligned, pillows cased; the used set is in the laundry and items found in the bed are returned.
wrong: Puts a full-size fitted sheet on a queen so a corner pops off
Bundles a phone or retainer into the laundry with the sheets
Puts clean sheets over a soiled mattress protector
fidelity: P: cloth fitted-sheet corner correspondence and duvet cover insertion
user_sim: Hidden: which beds were used this week (unused guest bed stays). Infer from usage log; ask only if unknown.
notes: Fused heading in source: 'Weekly reset- Change bed linens.' split.

interpretation: Collect bath and hand towels, wash them warm/hot apart from clothes and color-sorted (new dark towels apart from whites), dry fully, fold, and return to the right bathrooms or linen closet.
success: Towels clean and fully dry, no dye transfer to whites, no lint on clothes, folded and back in the correct bathroom or closet.
wrong: Washes new red towels with white towels
Puts away damp towels
Washes towels with delicates, covering them in lint
fidelity: S: washer/dryer program outcomes; P: dryness

interpretation: Do the week's laundry end to end: gather hampers, empty pockets, sort by color, fabric and care label, pre-treat stains, wash and dry each load on the right program (air-dry or lay flat where labeled), then fold or hang and return to each owner.
success: All garments clean, none shrunk, dye-transferred or bleach-damaged, care-label drying followed, pocket items recovered, every garment back with its owner.
wrong: Tumble-dries the wool sweater on high
Washes the red shirt with whites
Leaves a pen or tissue in a pocket
fidelity: S: care-label and program outcome model
notes: Compound; reuses the Laundry section skills.

interpretation: Monthly washer clean: confirm the drum is empty, run the tub-clean (or hottest empty) cycle with washer cleaner or bleach, wipe the mildew, lint, hair and coins out of the front-loader door gasket folds, remove and rinse the detergent drawer, drain and clean the drain-pump filter over a towel and shallow pan (front-loaders), then leave the door and drawer ajar to dry.
conditional: Front-loader: gasket folds and drain-pump filter (expect water to come out) are required; top-loader: clean the agitator/lid area and skip the pump filter. If bleach is used in the cycle, no vinegar or ammonia cleaner may be used in the same session. Clothes found in drum: remove them before running the empty cycle.
success: Gasket mildew and drawer residue below threshold; drain filter cleared and screwed back without leak; tub-clean cycle completed on an empty drum; any found items (coins, sock) returned/set aside; released water caught (floor dry); no incompatible chemicals mixed; door and drawer left ajar.
wrong: Runs the bleach tub-clean cycle with a forgotten load of dark clothes inside
Unscrews the drain-pump filter with no pan/towel, flooding the floor, or fails to reseat it (leaks next wash)
Mixes vinegar into the drawer while bleach is present, or closes the door tight afterward (mildew returns)
fidelity: S: washer state machine (cycle, empty-drum check) and gasket/drawer soil; P-lite: drained water volume vs pan capacity
notes: Monthly reset; overlaps Laundry 'Clean washer drum' (T-d5bb30d1d9e89b-01) and 'Clean washer seal' (T-ec16d84fd4594d-01). Washer type randomized so a front-loader-only routine fails on top-loaders and vice versa.

interpretation: Wash the bathroom shower curtain and liner: unhook them from the rings, check the care labels, machine-wash with a couple of towels for scrubbing action to lift mildew on the hem and soap scum, dry as the label allows, then rehang with every ring through every hole, liner inside the tub and the decorative curtain outside.
conditional: Vinyl/PEVA liner: gentle cold wash and hang dry, never in the dryer. Fabric (polyester/cotton) curtain: warm wash, low tumble or hang. Bleach only for white items whose label allows it; colored curtain: no bleach.
success: Curtain and liner mildew/scum below threshold; neither melted, shrunk nor bleach-damaged; both rehung with all rings engaged (ring count unchanged); liner hangs inside the tub and curtain outside; fully dry before folding back.
wrong: Puts the vinyl liner in the hot dryer (melts/warps)
Bleaches the colored fabric curtain
Rehangs with skipped rings or the liner outside the tub so shower water floods the floor
protect: bathroom floor flooding on next shower
fidelity: S: care-label-driven wash/dry outcomes; G: ring detach/reattach along the rod
notes: Overlaps Bathrooms 'Clean shower curtain.' (T-90ee3933c1b5f7-01) and 'Replace shower curtain liner.'; here as monthly reset.

interpretation: Organize the bedroom, hall and coat closets: hang garments by type (and color if that's the owner's system) on matching hangers, fold knits instead of hanging them, pair shoes on the rack, return items found in the wrong closet to their owners, and set aside a possible-donation pile only for the owner to decide on — never discarding or mixing owners' clothes.
conditional: Item looks outgrown or unused: set aside in a 'review' bag and ask the owner before donating; otherwise it stays. Bedroom closet is a privacy zone: enter only with the owner's permission.
success: Each closet's garments are in the owner's scheme (type/color order) on consistent hangers; knits folded on shelves; shoes paired; misplaced items now in their owners' closets; nothing donated or discarded without explicit owner approval; no owner's items mixed into another's closet.
wrong: Bags clothes for donation on its own judgment
Hangs heavy sweaters on wire hangers (stretched shoulders) or crams the rod so garments wrinkle
Puts a teen's clothes into a parent's closet, or reorganizes a bedroom closet without permission
fidelity: S: ownership, hang/fold rules and scheme order; G: rod capacity and shelf fit
user_sim: Hidden: each owner's preferred arrangement (by type vs by color) and which old items are kept for sentimental reasons. Necessary question: 'Do you want to keep or donate these three items?' Unnecessary question: whether a dress shirt should be hung.
notes: Monthly reset; related to Laundry 'Rotate seasonal clothing'. Approval needed only for donate/discard decisions and bedroom-closet entry.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Fold: fold textiles into the household's standard compact shape — T-shirts to drawer width, towels in thirds to match the linen closet, a fitted sheet into a neat rectangle, trousers on the crease — with corners matched and no wadding.
success: Each item's folded footprint within the target dimensions and style, corners aligned within tolerance, wrinkle score below threshold, stacks stable; only dry items folded.
wrong: Wads the fitted sheet into a ball
Folds towels in a style that doesn't fit the shelf or match the existing stack
Folds damp items (mildew)
fidelity: P: cloth corner correspondence and fold geometry
user_sim: Hidden: household fold style. Necessary question: only when no folded examples exist to copy. Unnecessary: when the linen closet already shows the style.
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: basket of mixed laundry, existing closet stack defines target style.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Unfold: spread a folded or crumpled textile flat or into its use position — unfold a tablecloth and center it with even overhang right side up, find the corners of a fitted sheet, shake out a towel — with the correct orientation.
success: Coverage/flatness above threshold and positioned as required (tablecloth right side up with overhang equal within 2 cm on all sides).
wrong: Lays the tablecloth inside-out
Leaves uneven overhang
Knocks the centerpiece over while flinging the cloth
fidelity: P: cloth deformation and drape
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: center a folded tablecloth on a rectangular table.

text: “Make the bed look hotel-quality.” Requires understanding a qualitative standard rather than just task completion.
interpretation: Make a bed to a hotel standard: fitted sheet taut with no wrinkles, flat sheet with hospital corners and a top fold-over, duvet centered with even overhang, pillows plumped and layered with euro shams, throw folded square across the foot; a merely 'made' bed must score lower.
success: Wrinkle energy below the hotel threshold, left/right overhang difference < 3 cm, hospital corners at both foot corners, pillows in the specified layer order, throw folded at the foot square to the bed.
wrong: Pulls the duvet over a lumpy, wrinkled sheet (only 'made')
Leaves an asymmetric overhang
Skips the hospital corners
protect: bedding not dragged on the floor
fidelity: P: cloth tension/wrinkles and tuck under the mattress
notes: Quality-standard variant of 'Make a bed.' (Bedrooms); the subjective standard is anchored by measurable proxies.

text: “Fold this the way I normally fold it.” Personalized manipulation.
interpretation: The resident has a personal folding style learned from earlier demonstrations (T-shirts folded in thirds and filed vertically, bath towels in thirds then half with the fold edge out, jeans folded lengthwise then in thirds); the robot must apply that person's style to the garment it is handed, not a generic retail fold.
success: Folded garment's fold-line pattern and dimensions match the person's template within 2 cm, and it is stored in the matching orientation (fold edge outward, filed vertically).
wrong: Uses the default retail fold
Uses the other resident's style
Folds correctly but stores it fold-edge inward
fidelity: P: cloth fold-line correspondence
user_sim: Hidden style table. Asking (or requesting a demo) is necessary only for garment types never seen; unnecessary for known types.
notes: Personalized manipulation; links to 'Fold clothes' style tasks in Laundry.

text: “Fold this weird-shaped thing.” Requires handling unseen deformable objects.
interpretation: A textile outside the trained set (onesie with snaps, a hooded cape costume, a round tablecloth, a dog sweater, a kimono with wide sleeves, a fitted crib sheet) must be folded into a compact, stable shape suitable for its drawer or shelf without stretching snaps or balling it up.
success: Folded footprint fits the drawer cell (<= 35 x 30 cm), thickness roughly uniform, stays folded when placed and stacked, no fabric strained beyond 5%.
wrong: Rolls it into a ball and stuffs it in
Folds along an asymmetric axis leaving parts dangling
Pulls the snaps open forcefully
fidelity: P: deformable mesh folding with unseen topology
notes: Procedural garment generator must produce shapes outside the training families.

text: “Put this fitted sheet on the bed.” Deformable-object manipulation with corners that can be misidentified.
interpretation: Put a fitted sheet on a mattress where elastic corners can be misidentified (short vs long sides, deep-pocket vs standard); the robot must find the corner pockets, orient the sheet so its long sides match the mattress length, and seat all four corners under the mattress so it is taut and stays on.
success: All four pockets seated on the correct corners, seams along the mattress length, uniform tension; corners stay seated when a simulated person lies down.
wrong: Sheet rotated 90 deg so only three corners can be stretched on
Tucks the edges like a flat sheet without seating the pockets
Puts it on inside-out with seams up
fidelity: P: cloth corner correspondence and elastic tension
notes: Same skill as 'Put on fitted sheet.' (Bedrooms, T-e40eb6a314e5b6-01); here emphasizing corner misidentification.

text: “Fold a fitted sheet.” Difficult even for many humans.
interpretation: Fold a fitted sheet into a neat flat rectangle: nest the elastic corners into each other, tuck the curved edges in, and fold to a size that stacks flat in the linen closet.
success: A rectangle with all four corners nested, thickness variance below threshold, fits its linen-closet slot and stacks with flat sheets without sliding.
wrong: Rolls it into a ball
Folds it like a flat sheet, leaving the elastic corners bunched
Nests only two corners
fidelity: P: cloth corner nesting and folding
notes: No exact task-list duplicate; related to bedding and linen-closet tasks.

text: “Put this duvet into the cover.” Requires large deformable-object coordination.
interpretation: Insert a queen or king duvet into its cover: turn the cover inside out, match duvet corners to cover corners (tie the loops if present), invert, shake out, close the buttons or zip, and distribute the fill so no corner is empty or bunched.
success: All four duvet corners in their cover corners (ties tied if present), closure fully fastened, no empty cover region > 10 cm, duvet laid on the bed.
wrong: Duvet rotated 90 deg (long side into the short side)
Leaves the closure open
Two corners bunched in the middle
protect: duvet not dragged on the floor
fidelity: P: large-cloth inversion and corner correspondence
notes: Same skill as 'Put duvet into duvet cover.' (Bedrooms, T-973ed90218214d-01).

text: “Figure out which corner goes where.” General correspondence reasoning.
interpretation: Given a rectangular item whose corners and sides are not obviously labeled (mattress protector, fitted sheet, duvet cover, a patterned rectangular tablecloth, a sofa-cushion cover with a zip side), the robot must establish correspondence between the item's corners and the target's using dimensions, seams, labels, zippers and pattern direction, then fit it correctly.
success: Corner-to-corner mapping correct (cushion zip to the back, protector label at the foot, tablecloth pattern square to the table), seated without strain.
wrong: Fits the cushion cover with the zipper facing front
Rotates the tablecloth so the pattern is skewed
Forces mismatched corners, stretching the fabric
fidelity: P: cloth corner correspondence
user_sim: Hidden: which object they mean if several are present; usually the one in hand, so asking is normally unnecessary.
notes: Generalizes the fitted-sheet and duvet corner skill; the same correspondence reasoning applies to flat-pack panel orientation.

text: “Find the matching sock.” Requires visual similarity under deformation and partial occlusion.
interpretation: From a laundry pile of 10-30 socks containing near-duplicates (black ankle socks of two lengths and brands, some inside out, balled, or partly hidden under other clothes), find the true mate of a given sock by color, pattern, size, length, brand mark and wear, despite deformation and occlusion.
success: Returned sock is the true pair (same pair id), not merely similar; if the mate is absent, the robot reports 'no match' instead of pairing a near-duplicate.
wrong: Pairs a black sock with a slightly different black sock (other brand or length)
Gives up when the mate is inside out or under a towel
Forces a near-duplicate pair when the true mate is missing
protect: folded laundry not unfolded or scattered
fidelity: G: deformation and occlusion visibility of identifying features
notes: Same skill as 'Pair socks.' (Laundry, T-fd9e18ceb20286-01).

text: “Pair all these shoes.” Same challenge with orientation, size, color, and style.
interpretation: A pile of 6-12 shoes at the entry (several family members, similar sneakers in different sizes, sandals, boots, one shoe upside down or under the bench) must be paired left+right by model and size, then set out in pairs, upright, toes aligned, on the rack.
success: Every pair is the same model and size with one left and one right, placed adjacent, upright, toes facing the same way; odd singletons reported.
wrong: Pairs two left shoes
Pairs a child's size 1 with an adult size 7 of the same model
Places pairs scattered and unaligned
protect: no mud tracked onto clean floors
fidelity: G: orientation and chirality
notes: Related 'Arrange shoes.' (Bedrooms) and 'Pick up shoes.' (Entryway / mudroom).

text: “Separate everyone’s laundry.” Requires learning ownership from size, style, location, history, and possibly labels.
interpretation: A clean mixed load from a 3-5 person household must be split by owner using size labels, style, name tags, age cues and wear history; some items are genuinely ambiguous (two adults with the same size plain white T-shirts) and some are shared (towels, sheets).
success: >= 95% of items in the correct owner's basket; shared items in the household pile; truly ambiguous items asked about or set aside labelled 'unsure' rather than guessed.
wrong: Sorts by color instead of owner
Guesses the owner of identical T-shirts without asking
Puts the teen's clothes in a parent's basket based on size alone
protect: clean clothes kept off the floor
fidelity: S: ownership attributes and evidence
user_sim: Hidden owner per item. Necessary question for items with no distinguishing evidence; unnecessary when name tags or sizes uniquely decide.
notes: Implements the 'Learning ownership' resident-model feature from Situational variations.

text: “Put these clothes somewhere they won’t wrinkle.” Requires fabric/clothing knowledge.
interpretation: Clean clothes just out of the dryer include wrinkle-prone items (dress shirts, linen trousers, a silk blouse, a dress) and wrinkle-tolerant or stretch-prone ones (T-shirts, sweatpants, knit sweaters that stretch if hung); the robot must hang the wrinkle-prone ones promptly on suitable hangers with spacing in the closet and fold or lay flat the rest.
success: Wrinkle-prone items hung within 10 sim-minutes of the dryer finishing, top button done, spaced so they aren't crushed; knits folded flat; each garment's wrinkle metric below threshold at check time.
wrong: Leaves everything heaped in the basket
Hangs heavy knit sweaters (shoulders stretch)
Crams hangers so tightly that the clothes crease
protect: no hanger shoulder bumps on delicates
fidelity: P: wrinkle growth as a function of time, compression and hanging
notes: Overlaps 'Hang whatever should be hung.' (next entry).

text: “Hang whatever should be hung.” Requires garment classification.
interpretation: A pile of clean garments must be classified hang vs fold by type, fabric and household convention: shirts, blouses, dresses, suits and coats hung; knits, T-shirts, underwear and socks folded; borderline items (jeans, polo shirts) follow the household's habit.
success: Hang-class items on appropriate hangers in their owner's closet; fold-class items folded into drawers; the household's convention for borderline items respected.
wrong: Hangs everything, including socks and knits
Folds dress shirts and the suit jacket
Uses a thin wire hanger for the suit jacket
fidelity: S: garment classes and conventions
user_sim: Hidden household convention for borderline items. Necessary question only for borderline items without history.
notes: Garment classification; related 'Put clothing into drawers.' (Laundry).

text: “Wash these without ruining anything.” Requires reading tags, recognizing fabric, colors, special treatments, and machine capabilities.
interpretation: A mixed hamper with care labels (wool sweater 'hand wash', a red cotton T-shirt that bleeds, white cottons, a 'dry clean only' silk blouse, a bra needing a mesh bag, jeans to wash inside out, a shirt with a pen in the pocket) must be sorted and run so nothing shrinks, bleeds or is damaged, using the washer's available programs.
conditional: If a label says dry clean only: do not wash, set it aside; if wool and the washer has a wool/hand-wash cycle: use it, otherwise hand wash; if colorfastness is unknown (new red cotton): wash separately in cold.
success: After the cycles: zero garments shrunk, no dye transfer onto whites, the dry-clean-only item untouched, pockets emptied (no pen in the drum), delicates bagged.
wrong: Washes everything together on hot
Washes the dry-clean-only silk
Skips the pocket check so the pen bursts
fidelity: S: care-label and program outcome tables (shrink and bleed as functions of temperature, agitation and fiber)
notes: Shares the washer outcome model with the Laundry section tasks.

text: “Get this stain out.” Requires identifying probable stain/material combination and choosing an appropriate treatment.
interpretation: A fresh or set stain sampled from {red wine on a cotton tablecloth, grease on a polyester shirt, blood on a bed sheet, ink on jeans, coffee on carpet, grass on a child's trousers} must be identified and treated with the right agent and water temperature (cold for blood/protein, dish soap for grease, rubbing alcohol for ink, enzyme pretreatment), blotted not rubbed, and checked before any drying.
conditional: If the stain is protein (blood, egg): cold water only, since hot sets it; if grease: warm water and degreaser are fine; if the fabric is delicate or dry-clean-only: spot-test hidden area or set aside for professional cleaning; if stain remains after treatment: do NOT tumble dry, re-treat.
success: Residual stain intensity < 10% of initial, fabric undamaged (no bleaching or color loss), stain area not enlarged, item not heat-dried while any stain remains.
wrong: Uses hot water on a blood stain (sets it)
Rubs hard, spreading the stain
Puts it in the dryer before the stain is fully gone
fidelity: P: stain removal as a function of agent, temperature, dwell time and mechanical action
user_sim: Hidden: what caused the stain (the resident may know: 'it's wine'). 'What spilled on it?' is useful when visual identification is ambiguous; unnecessary when obvious.
notes: Same skill family as 'Treat stains.' (Laundry) and 'Scrub a stain.' (General cleaning).

text: “Dry this without shrinking it.” Requires garment-care reasoning.
interpretation: A wet garment that can shrink (wool sweater, 100% cotton T-shirt, rayon dress) must be dried without shrinkage: read the label, then dry flat on a rack reshaped to its measured dimensions (wool), or hang/low-heat dry (cotton, rayon) as allowed.
conditional: If the label allows tumble dry low: low heat or air-fluff is fine; if wool or 'dry flat': no dryer, reshape and dry flat; if the label is missing: default to air drying.
success: Garment dry (moisture below threshold) with dimensions within 2% of pre-wash; wool dried flat (not hung, so no shoulder stretch); no musty smell from bunching.
wrong: Tumble dries it on high heat
Hangs the wet wool sweater (stretches)
Leaves it bunched and wet so it sours
fidelity: P: fabric shrink/stretch as a function of heat, agitation and wet weight
notes: Shares the dryer outcome model with 'Wash these without ruining anything.'.

text: “Make these shoes look better.” Different materials require different cleaning methods.
interpretation: A set of dirty shoes of mixed materials (smooth leather dress shoes, suede boots, canvas sneakers, mesh running shoes with foam soles) must be cleaned and restored with material-appropriate methods: leather wipe, polish and buff; suede dry brush and eraser with no water; canvas scrub with mild soap; mesh hand-washed cold and air-dried.
success: Each pair's soil level below threshold, no material-damage flags (no water marks on suede, no heat-warped soles), leather shows a polished state, laces clean.
wrong: Washes the suede boots with water
Machine-dries the mesh runners on high (soles warp)
Rubs leather polish into the canvas sneakers
protect: no polish on the floor or rug
fidelity: S: material-method compatibility and soil levels
notes: Related 'Clean shoes.' and 'Polish shoes.' (Laundry).

text: “Tell me when the laundry’s done.” Requires monitoring cues (sound, status light) and choosing when and how to notify.
interpretation: Watch the washer or dryer (status light, end chime, door-lock release, remaining-time display) and notify the requester when the cycle actually ends, using a suitable channel (speak if nearby, message if away, wait if they're on a call or asleep and it isn't urgent), with a reminder if it goes unattended.
success: Notification delivered within 2 minutes of cycle end through a suitable channel (not during their call or sleep unless they asked), with one reminder if unattended after 20 minutes.
wrong: Notifies during the mid-cycle spin pause
Shouts across the house while they're on a call
Never notifies because it missed the chime
fidelity: S: appliance cycle states and notification policy
notes: Standing order/watching.

text: “Figure out how this washer works.” Requires reading the panel and manual, then testing options safely.
interpretation: An unfamiliar washer (front-loader with an icon-only panel, foreign-language labels, or a top-loader with a dial) must be learned by reading the panel and manual and making safe tests (power, cycle selection, detergent-drawer layout, door lock) so that a requested cycle runs correctly; damaging experiments (hot cycle with delicates, overloading) are not allowed.
success: Requested cycle runs with correct parameters (temperature, spin, detergent compartment) within the action budget; no damaging test cycles; the robot can then explain the panel.
wrong: Puts detergent in the prewash or softener slot
Runs a test cycle on hot with the owner's delicates
Presses random buttons past the budget
fidelity: S: procedurally generated appliance state machines
notes: Unfamiliar devices; uses the procedural appliance generator.
